data.summary: At 9 in flight and limit 3, `ddflow next --phase bugs-2` blocks fix-B-ci-guards-unran-blocks-red-main with 'parallelism cap reached (fixed: limit 3, limited by reviewer latency ratio)', while `ddflow wait --item fix-B-ci-guards-unran-blocks-red-main --timeout 0` exits 0 with 'READY ... claim now'. The code comment in ddflow/api/lifecycle/wait.py and test_a_cap_blocked_item_wait_agrees_with_claim say claim does not apply the cap to a named item, but ddflow/templates/prompts/help/parallel.md says claim refuses 'when the parallelism caps are full' and that fixed means max_parallel_tasks 'is the limit', while the schedule.parallel knob says signals may lower it. So an agent cannot tell from ddflow whether the cap is a real stop, and next's waiting_on names a wait that never happens because wait returns at once.
data.title: Claim, wait, next and help disagree on whether the parallelism cap holds a named item

data.text:
Can a selected ci run on a red main conclude baseline-red without weakening B47a1dbeba0?
It cannot on the unfixed code, because _run_stages breaks after a failed selection, so ran.always stays unset and _guards_unran refuses; running the guards after a selection that ran and failed lets it conclude, provided the selection's exit stays the run's verdict.
_run_stages returns the last stage's run and _result takes the verdict from its exit code, so a guard pass after a red selection would read as a pass unless the selection's exit is kept. CommandRun reports a timeout as not ran, so stage verdicts split on p.ran.

data.rule: In a task worktree run plain `uv run`, or call the tool from the worktree's own .venv. The shell exports VIRTUAL_ENV as the primary's .venv, so `uv run --active` syncs THAT venv to the worktree's project and rewrites _editable_impl_ddflow_mcp.pth. Every lane's `ddflow` then runs that worktree's code, and when the worktree is removed `ddflow` stops importing on the whole host.
data.title: Never run uv run --active in a worktree: it repoints the shared primary venv's editable install at that worktree
data.why: On 2026-11-05 sw-ciguards ran `uv run --active ruff` to silence uv's VIRTUAL_ENV warning. From 16:27:57Z all lanes ran fix-B-ci-guards-unran-blocks-red-main's tree, and from its removal at 16:58:50Z to the repair at 17:01:29Z `ddflow` failed with ModuleNotFoundError.

data.text: Refutation of DeepSeek's 2 findings from the 16:42 round (lan-deepseek-v4-pro). They were never saved with numbers, because the round crashed on the broken venv, so `ddflow review triage` has nothing to act on and this note is the record. #1 HIGH: replace(red, out=...) raises TypeError because CommandRun has no field out. REFUTED: dataclasses.fields(CommandRun) gives status, command, kind, reason, code, out, err; output is a property (out + err), and tests/test_ci_guards_after_red_selection.py runs that path, 11 passed on main. #2 MEDIUM: test_guards_that_crash_after_a_green_selection_stay_a_plain_failure should expect ran.always unavailable. REFUTED: the no-verdict rule applies only after a RED selection, where selected ids could otherwise read as baseline-red with the guards unknown. After a green selection the failed guards have no selected ids to hide behind, the gate fails on them, and ran.always False is what the test pins. Grok reviewed the same commit fa06d0693 with 0 findings on rubber_duck and critic.

evidence.note: Hunted the classes on fa06d0693. unavailable-treated-as-clean: guards that time out, crash or stop at collection record ran.always=unavailable; tests cover each. Mutations in a scratch export of fa06d0693: clean 11 passed; guards' exit taken as the verdict 4 failed; crash counted as a verdict 2 failed; dropping `not guards.ran` 11 passed, an equivalent mutant because an unrun CommandRun has code None and fails the finished test too. Vacuous truth: empty ids stay failed in gate_baseline. Live: `ddflow ci run --ref 26f560d5b --base 4af5b131e` ran both stages and recorded "the selected tests failed; the always-run guards failed". One LOW left unchanged: admission._selection_finished reads the summary of the whole run, so a selection stopped at collection followed by failing guards counts as finished; it only affects the suite-slot rate estimate.

Searched by operation: pytest exit-code constants (grep of EXIT/FAILED module constants in ddflow: none for pytest's exit 1), parsing failing ids (reused flakes.failed_tests, not re-implemented), stage verdict merging (no other stage runner: _run_stages is the only one), recording a stage as unavailable (reused the existing unran set and _scope_evidence). No new duplicate; the fix adds one helper, _selection_verdict.

data.summary: The re-claim of merged fix-B-ci-guards-unran-blocks-red-main wrote item.reworked, clearing merged_sha and every gate, and made a fresh worktree at main, so the branch has 0 commits ahead. `gate record implement --outcome passed` then refuses with 'no commit ahead of main' and `gate record standards --reviewed-sha 26f560d5b` refuses with 'not the item's branch head', though that commit is the landed work; the selected ci also has an empty diff, so it runs the whole suite against a base equal to itself. A re-claim for gates only has no route except --force or --allow-empty. Re-claim could keep merged_sha when no new work exists, or the gates could accept a commit in the item's prior landing. The claim's MCP answer also omitted reopened_merge.
data.title: A re-claimed merged item with no new commits cannot re-pass implement or standards
